title: Wikimania 2026: lessons learnt and challenges for the future of free knowledge
content:
From 21 to 25 July, Paris hosted the 21st edition of Wikimania, the annual gathering that brings together the global Wikimedia community to share experiences, discuss the movement’s challenges and continue to shape the future of free knowledge. 

Under the slogan “Liberté, Équité, Fiabilité” (Freedom, Equity and Reliability), Wikimania 2026 addressed some of the major challenges facing Wikipedia and the Wikimedia projects: artificial intelligence, disinformation, governance, open education, the preservation of knowledge and the strengthening of communities. 

From Wikimedia Spain, Rubén Ojeda, Project Manager, and Jorge Jaramillo, a member of the organisation, took part in this event and share with us some of the lessons learnt and experiences they have brought back from Paris.

title: Countdown Begins to the Language Diversity Conference 2026
content:
The countdown to the Language Diversity Conference 2026 has officially begun, marking the start of an exciting journey toward a global gathering that will celebrate linguistic diversity, strengthen language communities, and promote inclusive participation in the open knowledge movement.

Scheduled to take place in Accra, Ghana, from 2nd to 4th October 2026, the conference is built around the theme “Strengthening Language Communities in the Open Knowledge Movement.” The inaugural edition is expected to welcome more than 100 participants from across the world, including Wikimedia contributors, language activists, researchers, educators, technologists, and representatives of organizations dedicated to preserving linguistic and cultural heritage.

The launch of the official countdown signals that preparations for the conference are well underway. It also serves as an invitation to language communities, cultural advocates, and supporters of free knowledge to look forward to an event that will bring together diverse experiences, ideas, and practical solutions for strengthening multilingual participation in the digital space.

title: Wiki Warriors 2026: Building India’s Indigenous Knowledge Equity, One Edit at a Time
content:
When a Language or Culture disappears, it is not just words that are lost. An entire world of history, culture, ecological knowledge, oral tradition, and collective memory fades with it. Preserving that knowledge is no longer a task for books and archives alone in the digital age, it means making it accessible to the world through free knowledge and digital platforms.

Wiki Warriors Training & Photowalk, Boli Cheto Foundation’s strategic programme to strengthen Wikimedia’s Knowledge Equity in India. It is a residential capacity-building programme that brings community members from historically marginalised backgrounds into the Wikimedia movement, not as subjects of documentation, but as its authors. Over 3-4 days, participants build the confidence, skills, and community to contribute to Wikipedia, Wiktionary, Wikimedia Commons, and related platforms in their own languages, on their own terms, about the knowledge that only they can bring.

title: Making Uganda’s Hidden Stories Visible: My Wiki for Minorities 2026 Journey
content:
My name is Atim Sally Ruth, and I contribute to Wikimedia projects as ASally Ruth. I am a member of the Wikimedia Community User Group Uganda and, in 2026, I had the opportunity to support Wiki for Minorities in Uganda as part of the Core Organising Team (COT), with a primary focus on communications. My fellow COT members were Sandra Aceng, Emmy Okwir and Emmanuel Oruk.

Running from 30 April to 17 July 2026, Wiki for Minorities brought together contributors and supporters around an important shared goal: strengthening the visibility and documentation of Uganda’s underrepresented communities, cultures, languages, and environmental heritage.

Uganda is home to remarkable cultural, linguistic, and environmental diversity. Yet much of this knowledge remains underrepresented online. For me, Wiki for Minorities is an important response to that gap.

title: 72 Hours Virtual Marathon Edit-a-thon in the Igbo Wikimedians User Group – July 2026 Edition
content:
The Igbo Wikimedians User Group’s 72 hours virtual marathon edit-a-thon once again advanced the mission of preserving the Igbo language through open knowledge, emphasizing quality contributions over sheer volume. Launched in April 2025, the project has achieved notable success thanks to community-wide collaboration and active participation. This edition in July 2026 built on the already established efforts and further strengthened editor’s skill.

We kicked off with our standard orientation session, helping participants get comfortable with the workflow and understand their assigned tasks. As organizers, we practically demonstrated translations on Translatewiki.net while re-emphasizing quality over quantity. We also showed how to correct reference errors, add the Databox and DEFAULTSORT templates to pages. From 28 to 31 July 2026, editors committed 72 hours to enhancing the Igbo Wikipedia. Throughout the marathon, participants concentrated specifically on:

  • Adding {{DEFAULTSORT}} and {{Databox}} to biography pages for better organization and accessibility.
  • Fixing reference errors in Igbo Wikipedia to ensure integrity.
  • Completing translations on Translatewiki.net

title: Wikimedia at Summer Institutes in Computational Social Science 2026 Uyo, Nigeria
content:
Twenty researchers, educators, health professionals, students, and practitioners gathered in Uyo with different research interests but a shared task: to learn how computational methods could help them investigate social problems more carefully.

For fourteen days, the Summer Institute in Computational Social Science Nigeria 2026 brought participants together under the theme “Tech for Open Minds.” The programme combined discussions on misinformation, gender bias, public health, education, digital inclusion, and knowledge inequality with practical training in data collection and analysis.

For many participants, it was also an opportunity to discover Wikimedia beyond reading Wikipedia articles.

The Summer Institute in Computational Social Science was founded by Professors Christopher Bail and Matthew Salganik, the SICSS Nigeria 2026 – Uyo experience was sponsored by the Templeton World Charity Foundation and Wiki In Africa. Hosted by Dr Rhoda Asuquo, with Dr Juliet Inyang and Yohanna Joseph Waliya as co-hosts. A handpicked group of exceptional facilitators facilitated each session, all experts in their respective fields.

title: Opening Access to Cultural Heritage through Digitalization and Wikimedia Commons
content:
In 2025, Wikimedia Indonesia, through the GLAM Indonesia Grant, supported several projects that bring together cultural preservation work with digital technology. This program is aimed at researchers, practitioners of art and culture, archivists, and communities working in the fields of galleries, libraries, archives, and museums. One of the program’s goals is to produce works that can be openly shared with the public through Wikimedia projects.

In its implementation, the two GLAM Indonesia 2025 Grant projects demonstrate different approaches to reopening access to cultural heritage. Illuminating Manuscript Ornament: From Royal Frames to Digital Commons processes the ornamental designs of Nusantara manuscripts into open digital visual assets. Meanwhile, the Digital Archiving for Banda Cultural Museum focuses on the documentation and digital archiving of a museum’s collection in Banda Neira.

title: How Learning About Capital Letters Brought Wikipedia Into My Classroom
content:
On August 19, 2026, I taught my Bahasa Indonesia class a lesson on capital letters, huruf kapital. On paper, it was an ordinary grammar lesson. For me, it was something I had been waiting for since long before I ever stood in front of a classroom.

I am a Wikimedian and an elementary school teacher from Indonesia. I have spent years believing in this movement, in free knowledge, in the idea that anyone can edit and anyone can learn. But for just as long, I have carried a quiet worry, that Wikipedia’s impact, for all its scale, often stays trapped inside the internet. It’s everywhere, and yet at the grassroots level, in a classroom, in a small village, in the hands of a child, it can still feel invisible. This year, as a brand-new teacher, I finally had a chance to close that gap myself.

title: Custom edit suggestions for every wiki: How communities are shaping Suggestion Mode with TextMatch
content:
Contributing to Wikipedia involves some invisible friction: finding content that needs improving, understanding what guidelines apply, and gathering the right context can all be effortful parts of the process. Suggestion Mode is a VisualEditor feature designed to reduce this friction while also helping people to publish constructive changes that they might not otherwise. It does so by proactively suggesting various types of edits one can consider making to improve content in an article.

Some of the suggestions apply broadly across all wikis, like detecting pasted text, inappropriately located external links, and images without captions. But what makes a constructive change can vary in practice beyond these shared cases. The patterns that signal a potential problem in an edit are rooted in the language, culture, and local editorial history of each project, and no single global set of suggestions can fully account for that diversity.

Rather than trying to solve this centrally, the Editing team is working to give communities the tools to define what edit suggestions would best identify these signals for their wiki.

title: Voices from the Bolivian Amazon: Madidi—My Journey to the Indigenous Communities Meeting in Wikimedia Projects
content:
EQUENE E QUEMA EJUDESHU TACANA IBUNEDHA

My connection to the Wikimedia projects began in 2024, when Eloisa Larrea Montaño, who coordinated editing workshops organized by Wikimedians from Bolivia, arrived in Tumupasa—a town located in the north of the department of La Paz, at the gateway to Madidi National Park in the Bolivian Amazon—with the goal of creating local content about the Tacana people from our own perspective and raising awareness of environmental conflicts, challenges, and projects we envision for our territory. The proposal was clear: that we ourselves, as the Tacana people, would tell our story on Wikipedia, including urgent issues such as the fires threatening our territory.

title: Six Months of Building Leaders, Bridging Knowledge Gaps, and Strengthening Community by Africa Wiki Women
content:
The first half of 2026 has been a period of remarkable growth for Africa Wiki Women (AWW). Across mentorship, leadership development, community campaigns, partnerships, and capacity building, our community has continued to create opportunities for African women to participate meaningfully in the Wikimedia movement while addressing the persistent gender gap in open knowledge.

Our work this year has gone beyond increasing contributions on Wikimedia projects. It has focused on building confident leaders, supporting new contributors, strengthening communities, and creating spaces where African women can learn, collaborate, and amplify their stories.

title: Wiki Loves Mingachevir: The Kyrgyz Wikicommunity’s Azerbaijani Adventure
content:
Held in the beautiful city of Mingachevir, Azerbaijan, from August 12-16, the Wiki Loves Mingachevir camp was an unforgettable experience in regional cooperation, knowledge sharing, and building new friendships. We represented the Kyrgyz Wikicommunity with a three-person team at this exciting event. Our participation was made possible thanks to a microgrant provided by the CEE Hub, giving us a fantastic opportunity to strengthen the bonds between our communities.

One of the highlights of the camp was the presentation on the Kyrgyz Wikicommunity, which I co-hosted with User:Ch. We shared our community’s past achievements, current general statistics, and exciting plans for the future.

The most beautiful aspect of Wikimedia events is that they offer not just a space for digital knowledge, but also for cultural exchange. To reflect this spirit, we distributed kurut (a traditional Kyrgyz dried cheese) to the participants at the end of our presentation. Tasting the kurut and the conversations it sparked added a very warm and welcoming atmosphere to the room.

title: Wikimania 2026: Impactful sessions, useful tools, and wonderful people
content:
I’m a volunteer with the Wikimedia Aotearoa New Zealand (WANZ) community, where I contribute to Wikidata, Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons. I’m also in the GLAM sector, as Curator Botany at Te Papa, the national museum of New Zealand. I attended Wikimania 2026 on an ESEAP Hub travel scholarship, and this blog is a summary of my Wikimania experience.

Wikimania 2026 was held in Paris, France from 21-25 July 2026. The theme for the conference was, “Freedom, Equity, Reliability (Liberté, Équité, Fiabilité). Together, let’s protect knowledge, equity and freedom.” About 1,200 people from over 100 countries attended in person. Sometimes there were as many as ten different and equally interesting parallel sessions, which made it difficult to choose which ones to attend. However, the sessions I chose to attend were articulate, well-prepared and worthwhile, and for I can watch those I missed on YouTube.
